question.problem: Use trial and error to find the solutions, if any, to the congruence $6x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,8).$
question.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=8$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7$ into the equation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cdot 0 & ≡0≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 6\cdot 1 & ≡6≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 6\cdot 2 & ≡4≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 6\cdot 3 & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & ✓ \\ 6\cdot 4 & ≡0≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 6\cdot 5 & ≡6≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 6\cdot 6 & ≡4≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 6\cdot 7 & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x≡3,7$ only $(\text{mod}\,8).$
